title.narrative: Second Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation Corridor 2 Road Investment Program (Tranche 3)

description.narrative: The proposed Tranche 3 will lead to improved road connectivity, efficient transport system, and effective management for the Uzbekistan sections of the CAREC Corridor 2 Road. The outcome will be improved travel time and efficiency on the reconstructed A380 highway section. The outputs of Tranche 3 will be (i) approximately 87 km of reconstructed Uzbekistan section of CAREC Corridor 2 Road (between Km 228-Km 315 of A380 highway); and (ii) nonphysical components for supporting the implementation of the civil works and for continued capacity development. Nonphysical components for this tranche include continued capacity development for implementing and updating road asset management system, and project implementation support.

description.narrative: Improved travel efficiency on the reconstructed A380 highway section.

By 2022, reduced travel time along Daut-Ata-Bukhara highway section (2009 baseline: 10; target 8.5) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The loan closed on 23 August 2021. The loan's financial closing date is 10 November 2021. Civil works progress reached 15.94% as of the loan closing date of 23 August 2021, with time elapse ratio of 36.1% (393/1096 days). Contract implementation will continue with the incumbent contractor and project management and construction supervision consultant, as per the contract signed under this loan.
The project experienced delays in procurement. Indicator will be assessed after project completion. Efforts towards achieving project's outcome are being exerted to put the project on track.
ADB received MIFT's letter dated 17 July 2021 requesting to include financing of remaining works on 87km to SRRP including retroactive financing. The government should also request ADB for direct contracting with the incumbent contractor and PMCS. This is important for the project team to seek Management and Board approval for direct contracting.
On 26 April 2021, ADB sent a letter informing the Government that ADB is not in a position to support the requested extension of MFF and L3355. MFF availability periods are, as a matter of ADB policy, limited to a maximum of 10 years. Extensions of the MFF availability period beyond 10 years are generally not considered, and if considered, it will be because of exceptional circumstances and will be subject to approval by ADB's Board of Directors (Board). Considering the limited progress achieved under L3355, CWTC is unable to present such extension proposal to our Board.
The project's latest approved closing date is 23 August 2021 which is the maximum allowable extension limit (10 years) beginning on the MFF approval date of 23 August 2011.
The Contractor continued construction works simultaneously in several sections of the project site. To accelerate the work progress, the Contractor mobilized subcontractors for various works, such as earthworks, utility relocation, bridge construction, and material transportation. Overall project physical progress as of 1 July 2021 reached 12.12% against the planned 17.96%. The financial progress is 09.01%. Time elapsed is 30.84%.
The civil works contract with China Railway 20 Bureau Group Corporation (CR20BGC) was signed on 15 May 2020, mobilized in July 2020 and estimated to be completed on 28 July 2023. The advance payment to the contractor was paid on 7 July 2020. The time for completion of civil works is 1,096 calendar days (36 months). Data Source: Periodic classified traffic reports of CR

There were delays in progress of works such as mobilization of personnel and construction equipment, utility reinstallation, material supply, site laboratory mobilization, etc. Due to COVID-19 lockdown, it further delayed the Contractor's mobilization and start-up activities due to restrictions on overseas trips imposed by the PRC Government. Output: Capacity for road asset management improved. Indicator: By 2021, on the job training provided to at least 50 persons of RRF and CR for implementing and updating road asset management system Achievement: n Progress/Status: As of the loan closing date of 23 August 2021, this RAMS component was not done under this project (cancelled).
On the job training not yet started but workshops conducted.
In November 2018, ADB conducted a 2-day workshop on road safety, weigh bridges and intelligent transport system (ITS). About 45 staff from SCR attended the workshop. The road safety workshop focused on the iRAP methodology and how its Vida software is used to systematically assess the safety risks on road infrastructure for all categories of road users. ADB will continue to support related capacity building activity along with road safety improvements, installation of ITS systems and installation of weigh bridges on its road projects. On ITS systems and weigh bridges, there were four presentations on ITS consisting of: (i) ITS Activities in Korea, (ii) ITS Planning and Policy Issues, (iii) ITS Architecture and Standardization, and (iv) ITS Service on National Highway. The presentation on weigh bridges focused on the introduction of weight station and Weigh-In-Motion (WIM) system and technology of South Korea and vehicle overloading problems and proposed solutions.
